title: How a Forklift Works in 60 Seconds 📦⚖️ #shorts
description:
A forklift is a giant seesaw on wheels. The front axle is the pivot, a heavy iron counterweight in the back balances the load on the forks, and a hydraulic cylinder pushes the mast up while chains carry the forks. Steering happens at the rear wheels, so it can turn in tight aisles. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#forklift #warehouse #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: A forklift is really a *giant seesaw*. Lift 2.5 tons, and the front axle carries almost *6 tons*.

steps.label: Lever
steps.text: The *front wheels* are the pivot. The load sits on one side, and the truck's weight sits on the other.

steps.label: Counterweight
steps.text: That's why the back hides a huge block of *cast iron*, the *counterweight*.

steps.label: Lift
steps.text: A *hydraulic cylinder* pushes the mast up, and steel *chains* lift the forks along with it.

steps.label: Stability
steps.text: It stays upright while its center of gravity stays inside the *stability triangle*, so keep loads *low and close*.

steps.label: Steering
steps.text: The *rear wheels* steer, so the forklift can swing around in *tight aisles*.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Pivot, balance, *lift*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
